companies.label: Meituan
companies.metric_name: Core Local Commerce segment operating profit/loss
companies.metric_basis: Meituan's own disclosed segment operating profit for Core Local Commerce (food delivery, Instashopping, in-store/hotel/travel), reported each quarter in HKEX filings

periods.src: Meituan Q2 2026 results filing + earnings call (meituan.com/sina/21jingji)

companies.latest_signal: Core local commerce swung back to a RMB5.7bn profit in Q2 2026 (margin +7.9%, up 11.1pp QoQ) as Meituan cut user incentives and delivery unit economics (UE) turned positive again; management attributed the swing explicitly to reduced subsidies and seasonal cost declines rather than demand strength.

companies.label: Alibaba
companies.metric_name: Alibaba China E-commerce Group adjusted EBITA (YoY change)
companies.metric_basis: Alibaba does not break out a standalone instant-commerce P&L; its own disclosed proxy is the China E-commerce Group adjusted EBITA line (Taobao/Tmall + Taobao Instant Commerce/Ele.me/Freshippo), where filings and calls explicitly attribute YoY swings to quick-commerce investment

periods.src: Alibaba June quarter 2026 results, CFO Toby Xu (SEC 6-K)

companies.latest_signal: China E-commerce Group adjusted EBITA fell only 1% YoY in the June 2026 quarter to RMB39.7bn, a sharp narrowing from -40%/-43% declines the prior two quarters; CFO Toby Xu cited improved quick-commerce unit economics while holding share, with management still targeting quick-commerce UE breakeven by end-FY2027 and overall breakeven around FY2029.

companies.label: JD.com
companies.metric_basis: JD's own disclosed segment operating loss for New Business (JD Takeaway/food delivery, Jingxi, JD Property, international), reported each quarter in HKEX/SEC filings

periods.src: JD Q2 2026 results filing + earnings call (sina/guancha)

companies.latest_signal: New Business operating loss narrowed to RMB9.85bn in Q2 2026, down roughly 50% YoY per CFO commentary, continuing a steady sequential improvement from the Q3 2025 peak of RMB15.7bn; CEO Xu Ran (许冉) described a 'clear profitability inflection' driven by delivery efficiency gains and revenue diversification rather than subsidy escalation.

war_summary: Regulatory pressure — SAMR's March 2026 'the delivery war should end' signal, its June 2026 draft rules barring long-term large subsidies, and Beijing-brokered 'anti-involution' talks in August 2026 where all three platforms agreed to cost-sharing and rider protections — forced a coordinated de-escalation from autumn 2025 onward. All three disclosed loss proxies have narrowed meaningfully off Q3 2025 peaks: Meituan's core local commerce swung back to profit and Alibaba's China e-commerce EBITA nearly fully recovered (-1% YoY) by Q2 2026, while JD's new-business loss has roughly halved but stays the largest relative drag. Meituan effectively defended share with the least sustained damage, Alibaba is absorbing the largest investment but improving fastest, and JD — still fighting for its ~10-15% share — is paying the highest marginal cost to stay in the game.
